name: A bastard's claim
about: A lord's child born out of wedlock comes to court with a token; acknowledged or denied, they rival the trueborn heir, or carry their grievance to an enemy house and come back with its banners.
title: The Bastard of {father.seat}

new.memory: My mother told me on her deathbed whose child I am: {father} of {father.house}.

goal.text: be named {father}'s child before the whole realm

fade: {bastard} drifts from hall to hall, and {thread} is told less every winter.

beats.speaker: bastard
beats.text: A young {bastard.man} named {bastard} rides into {hall} with a ring of {father.house} on a string round {bastard.his} neck, and asks for {father}.

memory.father: A {bastard.man} called {bastard} came to {hall} wearing a ring I gave a girl long ago.
memory.trueborn: A stranger came to {hall} claiming my {father.father}'s blood.

beats.speaker: father
beats.text: {father} looks at the ring a long time, then embraces {bastard} before the whole hall. {trueborn} does not.

memory.trueborn: My {father.father} put a bastard at our table and called {bastard.him} blood.
memory.bastard: {father} called me {father.his} own before the hall at {hall}.

beats.speaker: bastard
beats.text: {bastard} begins to say aloud what others whisper at {hall}: that {bastard.he} is the elder, and {trueborn} is soft.

beats.speaker: trueborn
beats.text: {trueborn} and {bastard} fight in the yard at {hall} with blunted swords that do not stay blunt for long.

die.how: I died in the yard at {hall}, by my {trueborn.brother}'s hand.

beats.speaker: bastard
beats.text: {bastard} stands over {trueborn} in the mud and lets {trueborn.him} live. The whole household sees which of them is the better sword.

memory.trueborn: {bastard} beat me in the yard before everyone and let me live. I would rather have died.

beats.speaker: father
beats.text: {father} must choose between {father.his} children. For a week {father.he} hunts alone and speaks to no one.

beats.speaker: father
beats.text: {father} names {bastard} heir to {hall} before the bannermen. {trueborn} walks out of the hall and does not come back that night.

memory.trueborn: My {father.father} named a bastard heir in my place. I was humiliated before the whole hall.
memory.bastard: I am heir to {hall}. My mother's boy, heir to {hall}.

beats.speaker: bastard
beats.text: {father} gives {bastard} a horse, a purse and a sword, and sends {bastard.him} away from {hall}. It is kinder than it looks, and {bastard} does not see it.

memory.bastard: {father} sent me away from {hall} with a purse, as if I were a debt.

beats.speaker: father
beats.text: {father} says {father.he} has never seen the {bastard.man} before, and has {bastard.him} whipped from the gates of {hall}.

memory.bastard: {father} denied me and had me whipped from the gates of {hall}.

beats.speaker: bastard
beats.text: {bastard} rides to {rival.seat} and offers {rival} a sword, and everything {bastard.he} knows of {father.house}.

memory.father: {bastard} has gone to {rival} with everything {bastard.he} knows of my house.
memory.rival: {father}'s bastard came to me with a grudge and a sword. Both are useful.

beats.speaker: bastard
beats.text: {rival} lends {bastard} men and banners. They march on {hall} with the bastard's own badge sewn over {rival.house}'s.

beats.speaker: bastard
beats.text: {hall} falls to {rival.house}, and {rival} gives it to {bastard} to hold. The {bastard.man} whipped from its gates now sits in its hall.

memory.father: My own bastard took {hall} from me with {rival}'s men.
memory.bastard: I hold {hall}. They whipped me from these gates.

beats.text: The walls of {hall} hold. {bastard} is taken among the wounded and hanged by {father}'s order, with the ring still round {bastard.his} neck.

memory.rival: {father} hanged {bastard}, who fought under my banners.

die.how: I was hanged at {hall} by my own {father.father}'s order.

beats.text: {bastard} takes a knight's place in {father}'s household at {hall} and seems content with it. {trueborn} sleeps with a knife under the pillow all the same.

beats.speaker: bastard
beats.text: {bastard} sells the ring in a port town and takes ship. Some say {bastard.he} will be back.

beats.speaker: trueborn
beats.text: {father} dies, and the question of {father.his} blood is left to the living. {trueborn} gives {bastard} until nightfall to be gone from {hall}.

memory.bastard: When {father} died, {trueborn} threw me out of {hall} before the body was cold.

bastard.text: make {trueborn} regret the night {trueborn.he} threw me out

beats.speaker: bastard
beats.text: With {trueborn} in the grave, {bastard} is the only child of {father}'s blood left standing. Whatever the priests say, {hall} will pass to {bastard.him}.
{bastard} is buried outside the walls of {hall}, where they bury those who are nobody's. {father} does not come.

memory.father: They buried {bastard} outside the walls. I did not go.
